I went to this place recommended by an acquaintance. I was curious about what it would feel like since it was a cafe directly managed by Kolonspo, but I liked that it felt less corporate(?) than I expected. However, calling this a flagship store of a complex cultural space may be frowned upon.
The first floor is well decorated with fabric-related props and interior elements to suit the location of Euljiro and a clothing company called Kolon, and when you go up the narrow stairs to the second floor, you can see that the feel of the place, with its different heights, space sizes, and finishing elements that are often seen in Jeoksan houses, has been well preserved. The divided space may be suitable for Kosi-guk, but it would be disappointing in terms of seat occupancy and operational efficiency. But don’t worry because it’s from a rich company~~!!
I was more satisfied with the Americano I ordered because it didn't have the franchise-like taste that these corporate stores often show, and the scent and aftertaste were quite good.
No matter who you go with, you will be satisfied with the basics. However, the seats on the second floor are uncomfortable, so please bear with them.

Since I only ate Guangdong Ssanghwatang or bag stick Ssanghwacha, I thought traditional Ssanghwacha would have a similar taste, but perhaps because there were so many ingredients, the herbal medicine-like taste of Ssanghwatang wasn't as strong. reviews.text:
I went to a craft beer pub to enjoy a quick aperitif with one of my companions before they arrived for a big drinking party. Actually, I suggested a different place, but it was far from Euljiro, so I came instead.

It is said to be operated directly by A&C Brewing in Hongcheon, which is similar to how Sokcho Craft Route operates a directly managed pub in Ikseon-dong. They also overlap in that they are both based in Gangwon-do.

However, the starting point is a bit different. While A&C Brewing opened a pub in the city center based on a brewery in Hongcheon, Craft Route started from a pub in Ikseon-dong and later established a brewery in Sokcho.

Anyway, coming back to the alien story, it was a bit difficult to find as it was located on the second floor of the building in a slightly speakeasy style. The group came first and I was impressed that they even prepared unexpected snacks for us.

Thanks to this, I quickly looked through the beer menu, and not only were there beers brewed by A&C Brewing, but there were also several guest beers from other breweries. I had my first drink of craft beer, Erste Pils.

As the name suggests, it is a pilsner, but it has a unique citrusy scent and emphasizes heaviness rather than refreshingness. It had an ale-like texture and aroma, reminiscent of Weizen, rather than a lager.

It wasn't my personal taste as it was somewhat different from Pilsner, which has a distinct refreshing hop flavor. Instead, the pizza was good except for the dough, and the synergy between the thick jambon, arugula, and rich tomato paste was excellent.

It's not appropriate to evaluate the dough since it's not a pizza place, but it had little moisture, was a bit dry, and was hard. Fortunately, the presence was lessened by the generous amount of Parmesan cheese and spicy wasabi cream.

Another hostess's corn tok was similar to the ones often seen at izakayas and tasted like sweet, sweet corn kernels roasted. It was savory and light without being overly sweet or strong in seasoning.

Next, the last glass of craft beer was a cherry ale, with a sourness reminiscent of red vinegar and a refreshing nuance with a subtle yet definite bitterness. It was a unique combination and I think women would like it for some reason.

P.S. The other pub suggested was Craft Roo.

reviews.author: 首尔外围Outcall&Incall
reviews.text: The hotel has a great location within walking distance and is very convenient for tourists. The staff speaks fluent Japanese and provides warm and attentive service, making you feel at home. The signature Cajun French fries are crispy on the outside and soft on the inside, and the Italian Spicy Sausage Pizza has thin, crispy dough and rich toppings, making it the perfect match for craft beer. The lively and relaxed atmosphere, with soccer matches broadcast on large screens, is perfect for Liverpool fans to gather to watch the game, and is the perfect place to continue the fun after the party. The spacious, modern interior is a bit on the high side at 10,000-20,000 yen per person, but it's well worth it considering the quality of the food, service, and overall experience. Whether you're a tourist or a local, it's a great place to enjoy delicious food, beer, and a sports atmosphere. Highly recommended to anyone looking for a quality sports bar, you'll definitely want to come back again.
